users.name: Aria Chen
users.bio: BCA Final Year student, frontend enthusiast, and coffee lover learning to nurture inner peace.
users.reflectionGoal: To balance project viva submissions with gentle emotional self-care.

journals.title: Project Viva Prep & Rainy Evening Thoughts
journals.content: Today was an emotional rollercoaster with our BCA project milestone presentation. The faculty asked tough questions about database normalization and API response latency. At first my chest felt tight and I thought I stumbled. But afterward, my teammate brought hot lavender matcha and we realized we actually passed all test cases! I feel relieved and proud of our resilience.
journals.analysisNote: Initial academic performance anxiety smoothly transitioned into warm gratitude and team solidarity.

journals.title: Overwhelmed by Endless Open Tabs
journals.content: I had 32 browser tabs open for React documentation, SQL schema tuning, and exam schedules. My head was throbbing by 4 PM and I felt like I was falling behind everyone in class. Took a 10-minute walk in the college garden and listened to soft acoustic rain sounds. Still feeling somewhat stressed, but taking it one task at a time.
journals.analysisNote: Expressions of sensory and cognitive overload accompanied by productive self-regulation through nature walk.

journals.title: Sunday Morning Sunlight & Fresh Berries
journals.content: Woke up without an alarm today. Sunlight was streaming through the sheer curtains creating soft golden patterns on my desk. Made strawberry pancakes and watered my tiny succulent plant. Did not open my laptop for 4 hours and it felt like my nervous system gave a deep collective exhale.
journals.analysisNote: High sensory contentment, presence, and joyful restoration through slow morning rituals.

journals.title: Late Night Doubts About the Future
journals.content: Could not sleep past 1 AM. Kept questioning whether I will get a good internship after BCA graduation and if my coding skills are adequate. Felt small and worried. Writing this down because keeping it trapped in my head makes the spirals louder.
journals.analysisNote: Anticipatory future worry and imposter syndrome expressed during late-night hours. Writing served as healthy release.
